crunch.description: A short-range trunk curl that brings the ribs toward the pelvis while the hips stay still.
instructions: Lie face up with knees bent, feet planted, and fingertips resting lightly beside your head.
Brace your abdomen and curl your shoulder blades from the floor without moving your legs.
Pause with the ribs drawn down, then uncurl slowly until your shoulders settle back onto the floor.
Keep space beneath your chin and avoid pulling your head forward with your hands.

reverse-crunch.description: A floor exercise that curls the pelvis toward the ribs instead of lifting the upper trunk.
instructions: Lie face up with arms beside you, hips and knees bent, and shins held above the floor.
Draw your knees toward your chest and roll the tailbone up using your abdomen rather than leg swing.
Lower the pelvis with control and return the thighs to their starting angle.
Keep your shoulders grounded and make the curl small enough to prevent momentum.

bicycle-crunch.description: An alternating floor crunch that pairs trunk rotation with a cycling leg action.
instructions: Lie face up with fingertips beside your head, knees bent over your hips, and shoulder blades lifted.
Rotate one shoulder toward the opposite knee as that knee draws in and the other leg extends.
Pass through center under control, then repeat the coordinated rotation and leg switch on the other side.
Keep your elbows open and rotate through your ribs instead of tugging your neck.

sit-up.description: A full trunk curl from the floor to an upright seated position.
instructions: Lie face up with knees bent, feet planted, and arms crossed over your chest.
Curl your head, shoulders, and torso from the floor until your chest approaches your thighs.
Reverse the motion slowly and place your back down from the lower spine to the shoulders.
Keep your feet steady and avoid throwing your arms or head to create momentum.

decline-sit-up.description: A sit-up performed on a decline bench, increasing the trunk's travel against gravity.
instructions: Secure your feet in the decline bench pads and lie back with arms crossed over your chest.
Curl your torso upward in sequence until you reach a balanced seated position on the bench.
Lean back under control and lower your spine onto the pad without dropping into the bottom.
Keep your hips anchored and use a decline angle that lets you control the entire return.

machine-ab-crunch.description: A guided seated crunch that flexes the trunk against the machine's resistance.
instructions: Adjust the seat and pads so the machine's pivot matches your trunk and your feet stay firmly supported.
Brace, then curl your ribs toward your pelvis while pressing evenly into the upper pad or handles.
Pause in the shortened position and slowly let the machine guide your torso upright again.
Keep your hips against the seat and do not drive the movement by pulling with your arms.

cable-crunch.description: A kneeling trunk curl that uses a high cable to maintain resistance through the crunch.
instructions: Kneel facing the high pulley, hold the rope beside your temples, and set your hips over your knees.
Curl your ribs toward your pelvis while keeping the rope fixed beside your head.
Pause near the bottom, then uncurl gradually until your torso returns to the starting angle.
Keep your hips quiet and avoid turning the exercise into a backward-and-forward hip hinge.

front-plank.description: A prone isometric hold that resists arching through the trunk from shoulders to heels.
instructions: Place your forearms on the floor with elbows under shoulders and extend both legs onto your toes.
Lift your knees and hold a straight line while gently drawing your ribs and pelvis toward each other.
Lower both knees to the floor with control before relaxing your forearms.
Keep your head aligned with your spine and prevent the hips from sagging or lifting.

side-plank.description: A side-facing isometric hold that challenges the trunk to resist bending toward the floor.
instructions: Lie on one side with your elbow below your shoulder and stack your legs and feet.
Lift your hips until your head, trunk, and legs form one line, then hold that position steadily.
Lower your hips softly to the floor and reset before changing sides.
Press the supporting forearm down and keep the shoulder away from your ear throughout the hold.

plank-shoulder-tap.description: A high-plank drill that challenges the trunk to stay square while support alternates between the arms.
instructions: Set a high plank with hands under shoulders, legs extended, and feet placed for stable support.
Shift as little as possible while lifting one hand to tap the opposite shoulder, then alternate sides.
Place each palm fully beneath its shoulder and finish by lowering both knees to the floor.
Keep your hips level and use a wider foot position if your torso twists during the taps.

plank-hip-dip.description: A forearm-plank variation that rotates the pelvis from side to side under control.
instructions: Begin in a forearm plank with elbows under shoulders, legs long, and feet close together.
Rotate your pelvis to lower one hip toward the floor, then sweep through center toward the other side.
Return your hips to a square plank and lower your knees when the set is complete.
Keep both forearms planted and limit the dip before your shoulders collapse or your lower back arches.

dead-bug.description: A supine coordination drill that keeps the trunk steady while opposite limbs reach away.
instructions: Lie face up with arms above your shoulders and hips and knees bent to form right angles.
Press your lower back gently down as you extend one leg and the opposite arm toward the floor.
Bring both limbs back over the trunk, then repeat with the other arm and leg.
Shorten each reach if your ribs flare or your lower back begins to lift.

bird-dog.description: A quadruped exercise that trains trunk stability during an opposite arm-and-leg reach.
instructions: Start on hands and knees with wrists below shoulders, knees below hips, and spine neutral.
Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back while keeping your pelvis square to the floor.
Pause at full reach, return both hand and knee beneath you, then change sides.
Keep the reaching leg near hip height so your lower back does not arch or rotate.

hollow-body-hold.description: A supine isometric position that holds the trunk in a shallow curve with the limbs extended.
instructions: Lie face up, draw your ribs down, and extend your arms overhead and legs away from your hips.
Lift your shoulders and legs from the floor while keeping your lower back pressed down, then hold.
Bring your knees in and lower your shoulders and arms to finish without abruptly releasing the position.
Raise your legs or bring your arms forward if your lower back loses contact with the floor.

v-up.description: A synchronized trunk-and-leg lift that meets near the top in a balanced V shape.
instructions: Lie long on your back with legs together and arms extended overhead.
Lift your straight legs and torso together, reaching your hands toward your feet at the top.
Separate the torso and legs slowly and return them toward the floor with control.
Avoid jerking from the shoulders, and bend your knees if straight legs pull your pelvis forward.

toe-touch-crunch.description: An upper-trunk curl performed with the legs vertical and the hands reaching toward the feet.
instructions: Lie face up, extend both legs above your hips, and reach your arms toward the ceiling.
Curl your shoulder blades up as your hands travel toward your toes while the legs remain still.
Pause at the top and lower your upper back slowly until the shoulders touch down.
Keep your neck long and avoid rocking the legs toward your hands.

lying-leg-raise.description: A supine leg-lowering exercise that asks the trunk to control the pelvis as the legs move.
instructions: Lie face up with legs together, hands beside you, and feet raised above your hips.
Lower both legs together with control while keeping your pelvis steady and your back supported by the floor.
Stop before your back lifts, then raise your legs along the same path to the starting position.
Keep the motion smooth and bend your knees to reduce leverage if pelvic control is lost.

hanging-knee-raise.description: A hanging core movement that lifts bent knees while the upper body stays quiet beneath the bar.
instructions: Hang from the station with a secure grip, arms long, legs together, and body settled without swinging.
Bend your hips and draw your knees toward your chest, finishing with a small upward curl of the pelvis.
Lower your knees until the legs hang beneath you and allow the body to become still again.
Keep your shoulders engaged and avoid kicking or leaning backward to lift the knees.

hanging-leg-raise.description: An advanced hanging raise that moves straight legs upward while resisting body swing.
instructions: Hang from the station with a firm grip, active shoulders, and straight legs held together.
Raise both legs in front of you without bending the knees, curling the pelvis slightly at the top.
Lower the legs slowly to a vertical hang and regain a motionless position before continuing.
Do not chase extra height by swinging, arching your back, or relaxing your shoulder position.

captains-chair-knee-raise.description: A supported knee raise performed with the forearms and back braced against a captain's chair.
instructions: Step into the station, press your forearms into the pads, support your back, and let your legs hang.
Draw your knees upward and curl your pelvis away from the back pad at the top.
Lower your thighs gradually until the legs hang beneath your hips, then settle before repeating.
Keep your shoulders pressed down and avoid pushing through your feet or swinging away from the pad.

ab-wheel-rollout.description: A kneeling rollout that lengthens the body behind a moving wheel while the trunk resists extension.
instructions: Kneel with the ab wheel below your shoulders, grip both handles, and set your ribs over your pelvis.
Roll the wheel forward as your hips and shoulders travel together, extending only as far as you can control.
Press the wheel into the floor and pull it back until it returns beneath your shoulders.
Keep your lower back from sagging and stop the rollout before your shoulders lose stable support.

barbell-rollout.description: A kneeling rollout using a rolling barbell to challenge trunk control through a long reach.
instructions: Kneel behind a barbell that can roll smoothly, place both hands on the bar, and brace before it moves.
Roll the bar forward evenly as your arms reach and your body lengthens from the knees.
Drive your hands down and roll the bar back toward your knees until your shoulders stack over it.
Keep the bar level as it rolls and end the forward travel before your back arches.

pallof-press.description: A standing cable press that trains the trunk to resist rotation toward the pulley.
instructions: Stand sideways to a cable set near chest height and hold the handle at your sternum with both hands.
Brace and press your hands straight forward, keeping your shoulders and hips facing ahead.
Pause with the arms extended, then draw the handle back to your chest without turning toward the cable.
Keep both feet rooted and adjust your stance if the cable pulls you out of alignment.

half-kneeling-pallof-press.description: A half-kneeling anti-rotation press that narrows lower-body support against a side cable pull.
instructions: Kneel sideways to a chest-height cable with the inside knee down and hold the handle at your sternum.
Squeeze the down-side glute and press both hands forward while your pelvis and ribs remain square.
Hold the extended position briefly, then return the handle to your chest before changing sides.
Keep your front foot and rear knee aligned rather than leaning away from the pulley.

cable-wood-chop.description: A diagonal cable rotation that travels from a high starting point toward the opposite hip.
instructions: Stand sideways to a high pulley, take the handle in both hands, and set a stable stance.
Rotate your ribs and hips together as you guide the handle diagonally down across your body.
Reverse the diagonal path slowly until your hands return near the high pulley, then reset your stance.
Pivot through your feet as needed and avoid twisting only through your knees or lower back.

cable-low-to-high-chop.description: An upward diagonal cable rotation that carries the hands from one hip toward the opposite shoulder.
instructions: Stand sideways to a low pulley, hold the handle with both hands near the cable-side hip, and soften your knees.
Rotate through your hips and ribs as you sweep the handle upward across your body.
Pause near the opposite shoulder, then follow the same diagonal slowly back to the starting hip.
Let your feet pivot with the turn and keep your arms connected to your torso rather than yanking the cable.

russian-twist.description: A seated rotation that moves the rib cage from side to side while balancing behind the hips.
instructions: Sit with knees bent and feet supported, lean your torso back, and clasp your hands in front of your chest.
Rotate your ribs to bring both hands beside one hip, then turn smoothly toward the other side.
Return to center, bring your torso upright, and place your hands down to finish.
Keep your spine long and reduce the backward lean if your lower back rounds.

weighted-russian-twist.description: A seated rotational exercise that carries a plate across the body while the trunk stays reclined.
instructions: Sit with knees bent and feet supported, hold a plate near your chest, and lean back with a long spine.
Turn your rib cage and carry the plate toward one hip, then rotate under control toward the other hip.
Bring the plate back to center and sit upright before setting it down securely.
Keep the plate close enough to prevent arm momentum and do not let the knees sway with each turn.

seated-medicine-ball-rotation.description: A seated trunk turn that carries a medicine ball across the body from hip to hip.
instructions: Sit tall with knees bent, feet planted, and a medicine ball held close to your sternum.
Rotate your ribs to move the ball toward one hip, then turn steadily through center toward the other hip.
Return the ball to your sternum and square your torso before placing it down.
Keep both sitting bones grounded and avoid creating the turn by swinging the ball with your arms.

standing-medicine-ball-trunk-rotation.description: A standing rotation that moves a medicine ball across the torso while the lower body turns with it.
instructions: Stand with feet comfortably apart and hold a medicine ball in front of your chest with soft elbows.
Turn your ribs, hips, and ball toward one side, allowing the opposite heel to pivot naturally.
Rotate smoothly through center to the other side, then finish facing forward with the ball at your chest.
Keep the ball controlled near your trunk and avoid locking the feet while forcing the torso to twist.

suitcase-carry.description: A one-sided carry that challenges the trunk to remain upright against an uneven pull.
instructions: Stand beside a dumbbell, pick it up with a hip hinge, and hold it at one side with shoulders level.
Walk with deliberate, even steps while keeping your ribs stacked over your pelvis.
Come to a complete stop, hinge to place the dumbbell down, and repeat with the other hand.
Keep the dumbbell clear of your leg and resist leaning toward or away from the loaded side.

stability-ball-crunch.description: A trunk curl over a stability ball that begins from a supported, gently extended position.
instructions: Sit on the ball, walk your feet forward, and settle your lower and middle back over its curve.
Anchor your feet and curl your ribs toward your pelvis while the ball stays beneath your back.
Pause at the top, then uncurl slowly until your spine follows the ball's surface again.
Keep your feet planted and hips steady so the ball does not roll away during the crunch.

stability-ball-rollout.description: A kneeling forearm rollout over a stability ball that lengthens the trunk behind moving support.
instructions: Kneel facing the ball, place your forearms on top, and align your ribs over your pelvis.
Roll the ball forward beneath your forearms as your body extends in one line from the knees.
Press your forearms down and draw the ball back until your elbows return near the starting position.
Keep your hips from leading the motion and stop before your lower back drops into an arch.

mountain-climber.description: A dynamic high-plank exercise that alternates knee drives beneath a stable upper body.
instructions: Start in a high plank with hands under shoulders, legs extended, and feet balanced on the toes.
Drive one knee beneath your torso, return that foot, and alternate legs at a controlled rhythm.
Extend both legs back to a steady plank, then lower your knees to finish.
Keep your shoulders over your hands and slow down if your hips bounce or your back arches.

trx-fallout.description: A standing suspension rollout that leans the body forward as the handles travel overhead.
instructions: Face away from the anchor, hold the handles with straight arms, and lean into the straps from a staggered stance.
Let your arms travel forward and overhead as your body inclines in one firm line.
Press down through the handles and bring your arms back in front of you to return upright.
Keep the straps taut and limit the forward lean before your ribs flare or lower back arches.
